features.title: Session Management (View & Logout)
features.description: Authenticated users can view their active sessions (IP, device, last activity) and terminate individual sessions or all sessions via a user_sessions cross-reference table (see ADR-006).
acceptance_criteria: GET /account/sessions lists all active sessions for the current user

User can terminate a specific other session
User can terminate all sessions ('logout everywhere'), invalidating all existing sessions
After 'logout everywhere', subsequent requests with old session IDs are unauthenticated
evidence: 5 functional tests (SessionManagementTest.php), one per AC: testSessionListShowsActiveSessions → 200 + <table> (AC1); testEachSessionEntryShowsIpUserAgentAndLastActive → .session-ip, .session-ua, .session-last-active asserted (AC2); testUserCanTerminateSpecificOtherSession → DBAL-inserted second row gone after terminate form submit (AC3); testUserCanTerminateAllSessions → COUNT(*) = 0 after Logout Everywhere + redirect to /login (AC4); testAfterLogoutEverywhereOldSessionIsUnauthenticated → GET /dashboard → 302 to /login via UserSessionRequestListener deauthentication (AC5)

UserSession entity + migration Version20260530170000 (user_sessions table: id, session_id UNIQUE, user_id, user_type, ip, user_agent, created_at, last_active_at); UserSessionRepository: findByUserId, findBySessionId, deleteAllByUserId (parameterised DQL DELETE)

UserSessionListener (#[AsEventListener]): inserts row on LoginSuccessEvent (guards instanceof User); removes row on LogoutEvent; deduplication: deletes existing row with same session_id before insert (prevents UNIQUE violation on re-login)

UserSessionRequestListener (kernel.request, priority -10): runs after ContextListener; if User authenticated but no UserSession row → $session->invalidate() + setToken(null); if found → updates last_active_at
CSRF: per-id token (session_terminate_{id}) on single-terminate; named token (session_terminate_all) on terminate-all; ownership check: getUserId() !== current user throws 404
PHPUnit: 169 tests — OK; Codeception: 128 tests, 385 assertions — OK; bin/verify-fast.sh exits 0; anti-cheat scan clean
Reviewer returned REVIEW_PASS (2026-05-30): all 5 acceptance criteria met; security review passed; framework conventions verified

features.title: auth-webhook-bundle: Retry & Delivery Logging
features.description: Failed webhook deliveries are retried up to a configurable number of attempts. Every delivery attempt (success or failure) is logged in a webhook_delivery table.
acceptance_criteria: webhook_delivery table exists with url, event_type, payload, status, response_code, attempted_at columns

A failed delivery is retried up to max_attempts times with backoff [Reconciled FEATURE-104/ADR-023: retry+backoff moved off the request path to Symfony Messenger's retry_strategy (max_retries 3, exponential backoff); the dispatcher is single-attempt (send()) and the handler throws on failure to trigger Messenger retry — verified by WebhookDeliveryTest::testHandlerThrowsOnFailedDeliveryToTriggerMessengerRetry.]

After max_attempts failures, the delivery is marked failed and no further retries occur [Reconciled FEATURE-104/ADR-023: exhausted retries land in the Messenger 'failed' (dead-letter) transport; the dispatcher logs one WebhookDelivery row per attempt — verified by testSendPerformsExactlyOneAttemptAndLogsOneRow.]

A successful delivery stops further retries and is logged as delivered [Reconciled FEATURE-104/ADR-023: a successful send logs status='delivered' and the handler does not throw, so Messenger does not retry — verified by testHandlerSucceedsAndLogsDeliveredOnSuccess.]
evidence: 4 functional tests (WebhookDeliveryTest.php): testWebhookDeliveryTableHasRequiredColumns → PRAGMA table_info confirms all 6 required columns (AC1); testSendPerformsExactlyOneAttemptAndLogsOneRow → HttpWebhookDispatcher::send() performs a single attempt and logs exactly one WebhookDelivery row (AC2/AC3 — retry moved to Messenger); testHandlerThrowsOnFailedDeliveryToTriggerMessengerRetry → the message handler throws on a non-delivered result so Symfony Messenger's retry_strategy retries (AC2); testHandlerSucceedsAndLogsDeliveredOnSuccess → a successful send logs status='delivered' and the handler does not throw, so no further retry (AC4). Reconciled to FEATURE-104/ADR-023: the self-retrying dispatcher/backoff loop was replaced by a single-attempt sender + Messenger retry_strategy (max_retries 3, exponential backoff); the prior testFailedDeliveryIsRetriedUpToMaxAttempts / testAfterMaxAttemptsDeliveryIsMarkedFailed / testSuccessfulDeliveryStopsRetriesAndIsLoggedAsDelivered were rewritten accordingly.

features.title: Fix: Add password reset link to login page (keep resend verification)
features.description: The user login page is missing a password reset link — it only links to 'Resend verification email' (app_resend_verification). The two serve distinct, non-overlapping purposes and must both remain: 'Forgot your password?' is for a user who has forgotten their password (reset flow, changes the password); 'Resend verification email' is for a user who knows their password but is blocked at login because their email is unverified (email_verification.mode=required) — they need a fresh verification email WITHOUT being forced to reset a password they already know. features.title: TOTP secret at rest: encryption intentionally NOT implemented (reverted)
features.description: Security review M1 proposed encrypting User.totpSecret at rest. Key and ciphertext always share the same backup/host, so at-rest encryption with a locally-stored key adds nothing while costing a custom DBAL type, a migration, Kernel wiring, and a flaky test. Decision: store totp_secret as a plain column. Revisit only if deployed on a networked DB with separate backups.

features.title: Fix expired-password change: verify current password + gate on real expiry (review C1)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C1 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). AccountController::changeExpiredPassword (/account/change-expired-password) sets a new password for the logged-in user WITHOUT verifying the current password (unlike changePassword, which does) and without confirming the password is actually expired; the route is also exempt from the 2FA gate (TwoFactorChallengeListener skip-list). A hijacked or pre-2FA session can therefore rotate the account password and lock out the owner. Fix: require and verify the current password before allowing the change; ensure a session that has not completed 2FA cannot use this route to change the password; do not weaken the forced-change UX for a genuinely expired user.

AccountController::changeExpiredPassword now (1) redirects a pre-2FA session to app_2fa_challenge BEFORE CSRF/any write (AC2), (2) redirects a non-expired user to app_account_change_password (real-expiry gate), (3) verifies submitted current_password via isPasswordValid before applying (AC1); template gains a required current_password field.

features.title: Login event listeners must filter by firewall (review C2)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C2 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). AuditLogSecurityListener, LoginHistoryListener, UserSessionListener and LoginNotificationListener never check the LoginSuccess/LoginFailure event's firewall name, so every stateless /api (PAT) authentication is treated as an interactive login: spurious audit login/success rows, login_history rows (API access logged as logins), phantom user_sessions rows (delete+flush+insert on a stateless request with an empty session id), and 'new login from unrecognized IP' emails on the first API call from a new IP. Garbage bearer tokens write unbounded failure audit rows and fire login.failure webhooks with no /api rate limit. Fix: each listener returns early unless the firewall is one of the interactive firewalls (user/admin).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four LoginSuccess/LoginFailure listeners early-returns for the stateless api and admin_api firewalls
A successful PAT authentication on /api writes no audit login row, no login_history row, no user_sessions row, and sends no login-notification email
A failed bearer-token auth on /api writes no login.failure audit row and fires no webhook
Interactive user/admin form logins still produce all of those side-effects as before
Functional test asserting an authenticated /api request produces none of the interactive-login side-effects
evidence: New src/EventListener/InteractiveFirewallTrait.php: const allowlist ['user','admin'] + isInteractiveFirewall(); the LoginSuccess/LoginFailure handlers in AuditLogSecurityListener (success+failure), LoginHistoryListener, UserSessionListener, LoginNotificationListener and WebhookListener (success+failure) early-return for the stateless api/admin_api firewalls (onLogout untouched — stateless firewalls have no logout route; LogoutEvent exposes no firewall name).

features.title: Deactivation / logout-everywhere must actually cut access: remember-me + PAT + stateless checker (review C3)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C3 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). (a) terminateAllSessions (AccountController) and the API forceLogout only delete user_sessions rows; the remember-me cookie re-authenticates on the next request because its HMAC binds only identifier+expiry+password-hash, none of which change. (b) The stateless api/admin_api firewalls have no user_checker and the token authenticators never check status/lockout, so a deactivated user's PATs keep authenticating indefinitely. Fix: invalidate remember-me on logout-everywhere; add a status+lockout check to the token authenticators (or a user_checker on the stateless firewalls); revoke PATs when a user is deactivated/deleted.
acceptance_criteria: After 'logout everywhere' (web and API force-logout) a previously issued remember-me cookie no longer re-authenticates
A deactivated user's existing PATs are rejected on /api (401)
A deactivated admin's existing admin tokens are rejected on /admin-api (401)
Deactivating a user drops their sessions and revokes (or causes rejection of) their PATs
Functional tests: remember-me after logout-everywhere; PAT after deactivation; admin token after deactivation
evidence: User gains a nullable sessionsInvalidatedAt column (migrations/Version20260706100000.php: ALTER TABLE "user" ADD sessions_invalidated_at DATETIME DEFAULT NULL, reversible down()); ConfigAwareRememberMeHandler::computeHash folds getSessionsInvalidatedAt()?->getTimestamp() (NULL -> 0, guarded by instanceof User) into the remember-me HMAC, so bumping it globally fails hash_equals on every outstanding REMEMBERME cookie while a fresh login re-issues a valid one — AC1.

AC1: AccountController::terminateAllSessions and API AdminApiUserController::forceLogout both setSessionsInvalidatedAt(now) + flush after dropping sessions. testRememberMeCookieDeadAfterWebLogoutEverywhere drives the real 'Logout Everywhere' form (incl. CSRF) then replays the captured cookie in a cleared jar -> redirect to /login; testRememberMeCookieDeadAfterApiForceLogout covers the API surface.

AC2: TokenAuthenticator UserBadge loader rejects status !== 'active' OR isLocked() (JSON 401 via onAuthenticationFailure). testDeactivatedUserPatIsRejectedOnApi asserts 200 while active, then 401 + JSON body after the status flips.
AC3: AdminTokenAuthenticator loader rejects !isActive() (status-only; admins have no lockout column per ADR-021). testDeactivatedAdminTokenIsRejectedOnAdminApi asserts 200 active -> 401 inactive.

AC4: AdminApiUserController::deactivate calls deleteAllByUserId(id,'user') + revokeAllByUserId(id) + setSessionsInvalidatedAt(now) + flush. testDeactivateDropsSessionsAndRevokesPats asserts 0 user_sessions rows, revoked_at set on the PAT, and the PAT then 401s on /api.
tests/Functional/Security/DeactivationCutsAccessTest.php (5 behavioural tests) covers AC5; RememberMeTest expiry-reauth regression watch holds (NULL marker -> constant 0, no behaviour change).

features.title: Admin REST API must write audit-log entries for all mutations (review C4)

All 12 mutating endpoints in AdminApiUserController and AdminApiInvitationController perform zero AuditLogger calls while every web-admin twin logs; a leaked admin token can delete users / reset 2FA with no forensic trace, though the spec requires the audit log to record admin actions. Best implemented as part of the C8 service extraction (FEATURE-103) so audit logging lives on one shared service path; if done standalone, add AuditLogger calls mirroring the web controllers with actorType 'admin'.

Audit rows record the acting admin identity, actorType 'admin', ip, action, and outcome

features.title: Cross-realm account lockout corruption (review C5)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C5 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). LoginRateLimitListener::maybeApplyLockout runs for any FormLoginAuthenticator failure including the admin firewall and issues UPDATE "user" SET locked_until WHERE email = ? against the shared login_attempts table. Admin has no lockedUntil column, so admins are never lockable, and failed ADMIN logins for an email that also belongs to a User lock that user's account. This violates the firewall isolation of ADR-003. Fix: scope lockout by realm/firewall so an admin-firewall failure never mutates the user table; decide explicitly whether admins get their own lockout mechanism or are intentionally excluded.
acceptance_criteria: A failed login on the admin firewall never updates the user table's locked_until
Lockout counting/keying is scoped so user-realm and admin-realm failures do not cross-contaminate
If admins are lockable, Admin has a lockout mechanism and AdminChecker enforces it; if not, the exclusion is explicit and documented
Functional test: failed admin logins for an email shared with a user do not lock the user account
evidence: migrations/Version20260706000000.php adds login_attempts.realm VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user' + realm-prefixed indexes; legacy rows default to 'user'; reversible down().

LoginRateLimitListener: realmForRequest() derives realm from path (^/admin => admin, else user); per-IP + per-account throttle COUNTs and the failure INSERT scoped by realm; maybeApplyLockout($email,$realm) returns early unless realm==='user' (LoginRateLimitListener.php:134) before UPDATE "user" SET locked_until — AC1/AC2.

AC3: admins intentionally not hard-lockable — explicit code guard + comment + ADR-021 (console-provisioned per OQ-001, no Admin.locked_until, account-keyed lockout is a DoS vector); admin logins still realm-scoped throttled.

tests/Functional/Security/CrossRealmLockoutTest.php (3 tests): 4 failed /admin/login attempts past max_attempts=3 leave shared user's locked_until NULL + recorded only under admin realm (AC1/AC4); shared user still logs in 302->/dashboard after admin failures; admin-realm failures do not throttle the user firewall (AC2).

features.title: Invitation resend resurrects used invites; registered email not bound to invite (review C6)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C6 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). Invitation::regenerate() nulls usedAt. Web resend (AdminInvitationController) has no used/expired guard; API resend (AdminApiInvitationController) guards expiry but not used-ness, so a consumed invitation can be resent and used to create a SECOND account in invitation-only mode. Separately, RegistrationController captures the invited email for display only and never compares it to the POSTed email, so any holder of an invite link can register an arbitrary email. Fix: reject resend when the invitation isUsed(); apply identical guards on web and API; bind the registered email to the invitation's email. Best coordinated with the InvitationService extraction (FEATURE-103).

features.title: Kill ALL recovery tokens immediately on deactivate OR delete + reject reset for inactive accounts, both realms (review C7 / ADR-020)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C7 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md), NARROWED by ADR-020 / FEATURE-110 (soft-delete). Original C7: password reset resolves the account by EMAIL at token-consumption time (PasswordResetController for users, AdminPasswordResetController for admins), so a stale unused/unexpired token issued to a since-deleted account could resolve by email to a NEW account created with the same email. ADR-020 makes deletion a SOFT delete (status=inactive; row and unique email retained), so a same-email account can no longer be recreated while the old row exists — the account-takeover vector is closed. What remains is hygiene, and it applies to BOTH realms (User + Admin): (1) when an account is deactivated/soft-deleted, invalidate its outstanding password-reset tokens (user password_reset_tokens; admin admin_password_reset_tokens) so a live link in an old inbox cannot act on it; (2) the reset-consumption flow must REJECT resetting the password of an inactive/soft-deleted account (an inactive account cannot log in per UserChecker/AdminChecker, so resetting it is pointless and a needless surface). Defense-in-depth: resolve/verify the token against the account's stable id at consumption, not email alone, so a stale token can never cross to a different account. THE PIN (Ken, 2026-07-06) — an invariant that holds REGARDLESS of any future soft-vs-hard-delete flip-flopping: whenever a USER or ADMIN is DEACTIVATED (status=inactive) OR DELETED by any mechanism, ALL of that account's outstanding recovery/login tokens are invalidated IMMEDIATELY — password_reset_tokens (user), admin_password_reset_tokens (admin), and magic_link_tokens (user). PAT/session teardown on deactivation is covered separately by FEATURE-098 (C3). This token-kill is driven by the deactivate/delete ACTION, not by row removal, so it cannot regress if the delete implementation changes.
acceptance_criteria: Deactivating/soft-deleting a USER invalidates that user's outstanding password_reset_tokens
Deactivating/soft-deleting an ADMIN invalidates that admin's outstanding admin_password_reset_tokens
The user reset-consumption flow rejects a token whose account is inactive/soft-deleted
The admin reset-consumption flow rejects a token whose account is inactive/soft-deleted
Functional test (user): deactivate a user, confirm an outstanding reset link no longer works
Functional test (admin): deactivate an admin, confirm an outstanding reset link no longer works
Deactivating a USER immediately invalidates that user's magic_link_tokens as well as password_reset_tokens
The delete action (soft-delete, FEATURE-110) triggers the same immediate recovery-token invalidation for both user and admin
The token-kill invariant holds whether deletion is soft or hard (driven by the deactivate/delete action, not by row removal)
evidence: NEW src/Security/RecoveryTokenInvalidator.php: invalidateForUser($email) bulk-marks PasswordResetToken + MagicLinkToken rows used; invalidateForAdmin($email) does the same for AdminPasswordResetToken (bulk DQL UPDATE usedAt=now WHERE email=:e AND usedAt IS NULL, idempotent).

Invalidator called at every account->inactive transition: AdminUserController edit(status=inactive)+delete, Api/AdminApiUserController update+delete+deactivate, AdminAdminManagementController edit(status=inactive)+delete (audited all setStatus() call sites; create paths correctly excluded).

Consumption gate: PasswordResetController::reset and AdminPasswordResetController::reset reject (GET+POST, before any password mutation) when the token's account is null or not active, rendering the reset template with token=null + 'no longer valid'.

NEW tests/Functional/Security/RecoveryTokenInvalidationTest.php: 7 tests / 18 assertions (deactivate+soft-delete invalidate reset/magic-link tokens for user and admin; consumption rejected for inactive user and admin with password hash unchanged) — genuinely fail on pre-fix code.

features.title: Collapse web/API duplication; collapse only dumb-data across user/admin realms (review C8)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C8 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). The mint-token/validate/email/audit logic is hand-inlined across the web and API admin controllers with observable drift (already the root cause of C4, C6, C13, C22). DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): (1) AXIS 1 — web vs API operate on the SAME model and MUST be collapsed fully. Extract UserAccountAdminService (create/update/deactivate-with-teardown/delete), InvitationService (send/resend with one used+expired guard), and a user-side PasswordResetService mirroring the existing AdminPasswordResetService; the web and API controllers become thin callers. This makes C4/C6/C13/C22 single-site and structurally hard to reintroduce. (2) AXIS 2 — user vs admin are DIFFERENT models and intentionally isolated (ADR-003); that duplication is a deliberate boundary and MUST be preserved EXCEPT for dumb data. Collapse ONLY: a shared trait for the identical reset-token entity fields/lifecycle (across PasswordResetToken + AdminPasswordResetToken, which also fixes the C32 getCreatedAt/strict_types drift); a shared trait for the identical PAT entity fields (across PersonalAccessToken + AdminAccessToken, owner-id stays realm-specific); the byte-identical reset-token repository method; and the duplicated ALLOWED_STATUSES constant (single source). DO NOT introduce a shared abstract service body across realms, and DO NOT extract a shared User/Admin identity base class or trait — keep those realm types fully distinct so a change in one realm cannot silently alter the other.
acceptance_criteria: Web and API admin user operations call a single UserAccountAdminService: one validation path, one audit path, and password-lifecycle bookkeeping (passwordChangedAt + history seed) on create
Invitation send/resend go through one InvitationService with identical guards on both web and API surfaces
The three inlined user password-reset copies call one user-side PasswordResetService
PasswordResetToken and AdminPasswordResetToken share a trait for their identical fields/lifecycle (getCreatedAt + strict_types drift resolved) while remaining distinct classes and tables
PersonalAccessToken and AdminAccessToken share a trait for their identical fields; the owner-id column remains realm-specific
No shared abstract service body across user/admin realms, and no shared User/Admin identity base class or trait

Web AdminUserController::new/edit/delete and API Api/AdminApiUserController::create/update/delete/deactivate are now thin callers that build an input array, invoke the service, and map UserWriteResult to their realm response (flash+redirect / form re-render 200 for web; 201/422/204/200 JSON for API). Actor identity passed in as (actorEmail, actorIp) so the service is realm-agnostic and testable.

Behaviour-preserving vs HEAD (diffed line by line): identical validation order/messages (email req+format+dup, name req, password req+policy, C22 role/status reject-not-coerce via shared UserFieldValidator, roles fixed to ROLE_USER per ADR-024); C27/ADR-030 UniqueConstraintViolation catch -> clean 422/200 never 500; C10 atomic audit preserved (entity mutations before wrapInTransaction, deferred audit row commits atomically; deactivate keeps its immediate log()); FEATURE-102 recovery-token invalidation preserved via a unified guard (status key present AND resolves to 'inactive', covering both old surfaces). AC6 realm boundary untouched — pure web<->API collapse within the user realm, no admin sharing.

The one intended behaviour change is the AC1 fold-in: admin-created users now get setPasswordChangedAt(now) + a passwordHistory->storeHash seed, matching the canonical RegistrationController path. Documented and tested.

features.title: Move email + webhook delivery off the login/request path to Symfony Messenger (review C9)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C9 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). Today LoginNotificationListener sends SMTP synchronously and HttpWebhookDispatcher makes blocking file_get_contents calls with a no-op backoff() inside LoginSuccessEvent/LoginFailureEvent, so a down webhook or SMTP outage hangs or 500s every login, and a password-spray forces outbound HTTP + a WebhookDelivery persist per failed attempt. DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): move BOTH email and webhook delivery to Symfony Messenger with a Doctrine async transport. (1) Route Symfony\Component\Mailer\Messenger\SendEmailMessage to the async transport so Mailer enqueues instead of sending inline — no listener code change. (2) Wrap webhook dispatch in a message + handler; KEEP the existing HttpWebhookDispatcher logic (SSRF guard, WebhookDelivery logging) but invoke it from the handler on the worker, not on the request. (3) Delete the no-op HttpWebhookDispatcher::backoff() and use Messenger's built-in retry_strategy (max_retries, delay, multiplier, max_delay) for real exponential backoff; exhausted messages go to the Messenger failure transport (dead-letter, inspectable/retryable). Doctrine transport chosen for consistency with ADR-001/ADR-013 (SQLite, single host, no Redis) and because messenger_messages lives in the same DB, giving transactional-outbox atomicity for free when dispatched inside the request's transaction. NOTE: this does NOT fix SSRF (separate finding C19 — the DNS-rebind pin must still be done in the handler); async only makes the call blind. The worker requirement (messenger:consume as a systemd worker, or messenger:consume --time-limit via cron) MUST be documented in README — without a running worker, email/webhooks silently queue and never send.
acceptance_criteria: A Messenger Doctrine async transport is configured; SendEmailMessage is routed to it so login/notification emails are enqueued, not sent inline
Webhook delivery runs in a Messenger handler on the worker; the login request only dispatches a message and never makes the outbound HTTP call itself
An unreachable webhook endpoint or SMTP outage no longer hangs or 500s a login (login succeeds; delivery is retried by the worker)
HttpWebhookDispatcher::backoff() no-op is removed; retry/backoff is Messenger's retry_strategy; exhausted deliveries land in the failure transport
WebhookDelivery logging is preserved (written from the handler)
README documents the messenger:consume worker requirement
Functional test: a failing webhook/mailer does not break the login response; the message is dispatched to the transport
evidence: ADR-023: email + webhook delivery moved onto Symfony Messenger with a Doctrine async transport (messenger_messages in the same DB); adds symfony/messenger + symfony/doctrine-messenger.

AC1: config/packages/messenger.yaml async transport = %env(MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN)% (doctrine://default?auto_setup=0); Symfony Mailer\Messenger\SendEmailMessage routed to async (enqueued, not inline). migrations/Version20260706120000.php creates messenger_messages (SQLite).

AC2: new App\Message\SendWebhookMessage + App\MessageHandler\SendWebhookMessageHandler run delivery on the worker; App\Service\MessengerWebhookDispatcher is the prod/dev WebhookDispatcherInterface binding and only $bus->dispatch(...). All four call sites (WebhookListener, LoginRateLimitListener, RegistrationController, PasswordResetController) enqueue unchanged. AsyncDeliveryTest::testWebhookDispatchEnqueuesMessageInsteadOfCallingHttp proves one message enqueued, zero HTTP.
AC3: request-side action is a pure enqueue (INSERT), so a down webhook/SMTP endpoint cannot hang or 500 a login; delivery + any throw happen on the worker.

AC4: HttpWebhookDispatcher refactored to a single-attempt send(url,payload): WebhookDelivery (retry loop + no-op backoff() removed, unused ConfigService dep dropped); retry is Messenger retry_strategy (max_retries 3, delay 1000, multiplier 2); exhausted -> failed failure transport. WebhookDeliveryTest::testHandlerThrowsOnFailedDeliveryToTriggerMessengerRetry pins the throw.

AC5: WebhookDelivery logging preserved — send() persists one row/attempt inside the handler; WebhookDeliveryTest::testSendPerformsExactlyOneAttemptAndLogsOneRow + failed-attempt-still-logs assertions cover it.
AC6: README documents the messenger:consume worker requirement (long-running + cron forms, DSN, failed transport).
AC7: tests/Functional/Messenger/AsyncDeliveryTest.php covers async routing + enqueue; SendEmailMessage resolves to a sender.

Test wiring: when@test routes SendEmailMessage -> sync:// (MailerAssertionsTrait still counts sent), async/failed -> in-memory:// (inspectable); WebhookDispatcherInterface stays InMemoryWebhookDispatcher in test/acceptance; config/packages/acceptance/messenger.yaml -> sync:// (no worker on live server).

Reviewer independently re-ran AsyncDeliveryTest + WebhookDeliveryTest -> OK (6 tests, 21 assertions); regression watch (WebhookTest, ApiLoginSideEffectsTest, LoginNotificationTest, WebhookSsrfGuardTest, EmailVerificationTest, MagicLinkTest) -> OK (39 tests, 99 assertions).

features.title: Harden webhook SSRF guard: hard-coded IPv4+IPv6 private/reserved blocklist, resolve-check-bind-per-call, no redirects, default-ON switch (review C19)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C19 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). The current HttpWebhookDispatcher::isAllowedUrl() has a DNS-rebind TOCTOU (resolves for the check, then file_get_contents re-resolves independently at connect) and does not cover IPv6. DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): keep a hard-coded (in-code, not admin-editable) blocklist of private/reserved/link-local ranges for BOTH IPv4 and IPv6, and gate the whole guard behind a config switch that is ON by default. Threat-model context: this deployment is single-host / no cloud, so the flashiest payoff (cloud-metadata credential theft) is reduced, but default-ON still protects localhost/LAN internal services here and keeps forks safe if this is ever deployed on a cloud or made multi-tenant; an operator who knowingly needs internal webhook delivery can turn the switch OFF. Guard mechanics (fixes the TOCTOU): on EACH delivery, resolve the target host to ALL addresses (A + AAAA), reject if ANY resolved address falls in a blocked range, then BIND the connection to a validated address (e.g. cURL CURLOPT_RESOLVE) so the call cannot re-resolve to a different IP; keep the Host header = original hostname so TLS/SNI/vhost still work. Refuse HTTP redirects outright (a 302 to an internal host would otherwise re-open the hole with a fresh unchecked name). IPv6 must include the embedded-IPv4 bypass forms: unwrap IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and Teredo (2001::/32) and check the embedded IPv4 against the IPv4 blocklist too. Beyond IP-range checks, reject any webhook target that is not a public FQDN: single-label hostnames with no TLD (localhost, intranet, db, router, etc. — which resolve internally via DNS search domains, /etc/hosts or mDNS) and special-use/internal TLDs (.local, .internal, .localhost, .home.arpa, .lan, .corp) are banned, since a legitimate webhook endpoint is always a public FQDN. This guard lives in the webhook delivery path and applies whether delivery is sync or via the Messenger handler (FEATURE-104).

features.title: Fix flush() footguns: scope audit + session writes, commit success-audit atomically with the business change (review C10)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C10 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). AuditLogger::log() and UserSessionRequestListener both call a bare $em->flush(), which commits the ENTIRE unit of work: (A) collateral commit — any entity dirtied earlier in the request is silently persisted when an unrelated logging/session write flushes; (B) the audit row commits immediately and independently, so an audit 'success' can be written BEFORE the business change it describes, and if that change later fails/rolls back the log records an action that never happened. DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): (1) For the success-of-a-business-change case, AuditLogger::log() must NOT call flush(); it persist()s the entry and the CALLER owns a single transaction boundary (prefer em->wrapInTransaction) so the audit row and the business change commit atomically — both or neither. This fixes A (no surprise flush from a logging call) and B in its strongest form: no false-positive 'success' AND no missing entry from a crash-after-commit gap (logging merely 'after' commit would still leave that gap). (2) DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: events that must be recorded regardless of a rolled-back business change — login success/failure, security events, explicit 'failure' outcomes — get an independent write that survives the rollback (dedicated DBAL insert / separate connection). So the rule is: success-of-a-change = atomic with the change; failure/security/login = independent durable write. (3) UserSessionRequestListener's last_active_at bump must be a scoped DBAL UPDATE of that one row (not a whole-UoW flush) and should be throttled (e.g. write at most every N seconds, not on every request) to avoid a per-request write — important on SQLite (single-writer whole-DB lock); the session-existence check that enforces terminated-session logout must still run on every request.
acceptance_criteria: AuditLogger no longer issues a bare $em->flush() that commits the whole unit of work for success-of-a-business-change logs

Login/security/explicit-failure audit events are still recorded even when a surrounding business change rolls back (independent durable write)
No unrelated dirty entity is committed as a side effect of a logging or session-activity write

UserSessionRequestListener updates last_active_at via a scoped write (not a full-UoW flush) and throttles it (not every request), while STILL checking session existence on every request so terminated-session logout is unaffected
Test: a forced failure in an admin mutation leaves no 'success' audit row for that action
Test: a login failure still writes its audit row
evidence: AuditLogger::log() rewritten as an independent, autocommit DBAL Connection::insert('audit_log', ...) — never persist()/flush()es the unit of work; new logDeferred() is persist-only (no flush) for atomic callers. Enum guard preserved (log() via assertValid(); logDeferred() via entity setters).

AC1/AC4: tests/Functional/AuditLog/AuditFlushFootgunTest.php::testLoggingDoesNotCommitUnrelatedDirtyEntity — a managed User dirtied in memory is NOT committed by a log() call, while the audit row itself IS written; fails on the old flush-based log().

AC2/AC6: testBusinessRollbackLeavesNoSuccessAuditRow — em->wrapInTransaction(persist user + logDeferred 'admin.user_create' success) then throw leaves neither user nor audit row. Admin web+API create/update/delete wrap logDeferred() in wrapInTransaction; create paths' UniqueConstraintViolation catch wraps the transaction.

features.title: Decouple login-notification recognition from the history-write race + shared fingerprint helper (review C14)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C14 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). LoginNotificationListener (priority 10) and LoginHistoryListener (implicit priority 0) both fire on LoginSuccessEvent and both compute hash('sha256', $ip . $userAgent) verbatim. The notification 'is this device known?' check (LoginNotificationListener.php:43-49) queries login_history — the SAME table LoginHistoryListener writes the current login into — so the feature only works because notification happens to run BEFORE history inserts; reorder them (give history priority >= 10, or a refactor) and the current login matches its own freshly-inserted fingerprint, so every device looks 'known' and alerts silently stop, with no error and no failing test. Separately, the duplicated formula must stay byte-identical across both files or recognition breaks (any drift => a 'new login' email on every login). ROOT CAUSE (Ken, 2026-07-06): one value — the fingerprint stored in login_history — is overloaded for TWO jobs (recording login history AND driving notification recognition), and that overloading is what couples the two listeners via run-order. DECISION (Ken — record as an ADR when picked up): (1) Extract the fingerprint computation into ONE shared helper that both listeners call, so the formula is defined once and cannot drift. (2) Decouple recognition from the history-write ordering by tracking notification state INDEPENDENTLY: the notification decision consults a dedicated 'have we already notified this user for this device' marker (e.g. a login_notification_seen record keyed on user_id + fingerprint, or + ip under ip_only mode) rather than inferring recognition from the login_history table the other listener races on — send iff no such marker exists, then record the marker. This removes the load-bearing listener-priority coupling entirely; the listeners can then run in any order. (Acceptable alternative if a marker store is unwanted: keep reading history but explicitly EXCLUDE the current login from the query AND pin LoginHistoryListener to an explicit, commented priority below the notifier.) (2b) ADDITIONALLY (Ken): when an alert IS sent, also write a dedicated audit_log row (action 'login_notification_sent') so the trail plainly shows it — but this audit row is for VISIBILITY ONLY and MUST NOT be the recognition source of truth. Using the audit log as the marker would re-overload one store with two states (audit trail + recognition memory) — the exact anti-pattern this fix removes — and would couple recognition to audit-retention pruning (prune the row => device looks new => spurious re-alert), on top of audit_log being unindexed (full scan per login, finding C30). So the recognition marker and the audit row stay two separate single-purpose records: the marker answers 'have we alerted this device?', the audit row records 'we alerted, for the trail'. (3) Add a test tripwire: two successive logins from the same device => the second must NOT notify — this single test catches both an ordering regression and a formula drift. MIGRATION NOTE: seed the marker store from existing login_history (or apply a one-time grace) so users are not alerted about devices they have long used the first time this ships.
acceptance_criteria: A single shared fingerprint helper is used by both LoginNotificationListener and LoginHistoryListener; the hash formula is defined in exactly one place

The 'known device / should notify' decision does not depend on whether LoginHistoryListener has already run for this request (no listener-priority coupling); reordering the two listeners does not change notification behaviour
First login from a new device notifies; a subsequent login from the same device does not
recognition_mode (ip_only vs fingerprint) is still honoured by the decoupled check

When an alert is sent a dedicated audit_log row (action 'login_notification_sent') is written for transparency; recognition state is NOT read from the audit log (kept separate so audit retention/pruning cannot affect notification behaviour)
Existing devices are not spuriously alerted on first deploy (marker store seeded from history, or a documented grace)
Test tripwire: two successive logins from the same device produce exactly one (first-time) notification; a login from a new device notifies again
No 'notify on every login' regression is possible from the fingerprint formula, since it now has a single source
evidence: ADR-031: recognition moved to a dedicated single-purpose marker store (login_notification_seen, UNIQUE(user_id, marker)); recognition never reads login_history, removing the listener-priority coupling.

src/Entity/LoginNotificationSeen.php + Repository (hasSeen/markSeen, swallows UniqueConstraintViolationException per ADR-030); marker = ip_only ? ip : fingerprint, honouring recognition_mode (AC4).

migrations/Version20260706160000.php — creates login_notification_seen + named indexes and seeds from login_history (DISTINCT user_id+fingerprint AND user_id+ip) so existing devices aren't spuriously alerted on deploy (AC6).
LoginNotificationListener writes a dedicated audit_log row (action 'login_notification_sent', outcome 'success') for visibility only; recognition stays on the marker store (AC5).

features.title: Admin login notifications — new-device email alerts for admins (separate table, mirrors user side)
features.description: ENHANCEMENT beyond the original spec (SPEC frames Login Notifications and Login History as USER features; LoginNotificationListener and LoginHistoryListener both bail on non-User, so admins currently get no login alerts). DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): admins should ALSO receive 'new login from an unrecognized device' emails. Build the admin-side mirror of the user login-notification flow, following ADR-003 realm isolation and Ken's explicit-separation preference. An admin-firewall LoginSuccess handler, for Admin logins, computes the device fingerprint via the SHARED helper introduced in FEATURE-107 (single formula across user + admin), checks a DEDICATED admin_login_notification_seen table (a SEPARATE table — NOT a shared table with a user_type discriminator; mirrors the token-table pairs like admin_password_reset_tokens; owner column is admin_id; the identical columns are shared with the user table via a trait, per the C8 dumb-data rule), emails the admin on an unrecognized device, then records the marker. Reuse the same recognition_mode semantics (fingerprint / ip_only). Also write a 'login_notification_sent' audit row (actorType 'admin') for visibility, kept SEPARATE from the recognition marker (recognition is never read from the audit log — per FEATURE-107). CONFIG: prefer explicit admin-specific keys (e.g. login_notifications.admin_enabled + admin_recognition_mode) over silently reusing the user keys, consistent with the explicit-over-clever preference; confirm as an OQ/ADR at implementation. OUT OF SCOPE here: admin login-history (the 'view your recent logins' parity) is a separate item and is not required for notifications, since the decoupled design recognizes devices via the marker table, not login_history.

The device fingerprint is computed via the shared helper from FEATURE-107 (one formula across user and admin)

features.title: User AND admin deletion is soft-delete (status=inactive), never a hard row removal (ADR-020)
features.description: DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — ADR-020): no right-to-erasure; history is retained indefinitely for replayability and lingering PII (IPs/UAs) is explicitly accepted. 'Deleting' a user must be a SOFT delete = set status='inactive' (disabled, cannot authenticate) reusing the EXISTING active/inactive status field — NO new 'archived' state, NO archived_at, NO schema change. The defect: AdminUserController::delete (:154) and Api/AdminApiUserController (:185) currently call $em->remove($user); $em->flush(); which PHYSICALLY erases the users row (hard delete) and — there are no DB foreign keys anywhere, every satellite table keys on a scalar user_id/email — strands login_history/password_history/user_sessions/tokens against an id that no longer resolves. Swap the remove() for $user->setStatus('inactive') + flush() in both the web and API delete actions; the row and its history stay intact. Reframes review finding C11 (orphan-on-delete is resolved by not deleting; C7 PII-lingering is moot by policy). Confirm login already rejects non-active accounts. ADMIN PARITY (Ken, 2026-07-06): the SAME applies to admins — the admin delete action (AdminAdminManagementController) must likewise SOFT-delete by setting the Admin's status='inactive' (reusing Admin.status / isActive), never EntityManager::remove; a soft-deleted admin cannot authenticate on the admin firewall.

features.title: Combined maintenance prune command for expired/used ephemeral tokens + dead user_sessions (ADR-020)
features.description: DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — ADR-020): historical data is retained forever, but genuinely EPHEMERAL security artifacts (no historical value, unbounded growth is a hygiene/availability problem) must be flushed on a schedule. Today only app:audit-log:prune (AuditLogPruneCommand) exists and nothing is scheduled (no Symfony Scheduler, no repo crontab). Add ONE combined console command (app:maintenance:prune) that deletes: expired OR used password_reset_tokens and admin_password_reset_tokens; expired OR used magic_link_tokens; and expired user_sessions (today removed ONLY on explicit logout, so dead rows accumulate forever and show as phantom rows in the 'Active Sessions' view). Follows the ADR-008 pattern — the command is the mechanism; operators cron it. Does NOT touch login_history, password_history, or audit_log (retained by policy). This is the only surviving remnant of review finding C11.
acceptance_criteria: A single combined command app:maintenance:prune exists (mirrors AuditLogPruneCommand's structure)
It deletes expired OR already-used rows from password_reset_tokens and admin_password_reset_tokens
It deletes expired OR already-used rows from magic_link_tokens
It deletes expired user_sessions rows (rows whose lifetime has elapsed), independent of explicit logout
It NEVER deletes from login_history, password_history, or audit_log (retention by policy)
The command reports counts removed per table and is safely re-runnable (idempotent)

Functional/integration test: seed expired+used tokens and an expired user_session, run the command, assert those rows are gone and that a fresh/valid token, a valid session, and a login_history row all survive

features.title: Mark the trusted-device 2FA-bypass cookie Secure via request->isSecure() (review C15)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C15 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). TrustedDeviceManager (src/Security/TrustedDeviceManager.php:24-34) hardcodes the cookie's $secure flag to false, so the Secure attribute is NEVER set — not even on production HTTPS. This cookie is a bearer credential that SKIPS the entire 2FA challenge, so leaking it lets a network attacker bypass 2FA on that device. The sibling remember-me cookie already derives Secure from $request->isSecure() (ConfigAwareRememberMeHandler); this one is an unhardened inconsistency. This matters specifically here because the deployment enforces HTTPS via REDIRECT and does NOT use HSTS (Ken, 2026-07-06): the http->https redirect fires only AFTER the browser has already attached and sent the cookie on the initial plaintext request (or under an SSL-strip MITM), so without Secure the 2FA-bypass token leaks on the wire before the redirect can help. FIX: set $secure from $request->isSecure() (mirror the remember-me handler) — true on HTTPS so Secure is emitted, false on local http so the cookie still works for local testing (no regression). While here, confirm HttpOnly and SameSite are set consistent with the session/remember-me cookies.
acceptance_criteria: The trusted-device cookie's Secure flag is derived from $request->isSecure(), not hardcoded false
On an HTTPS request the cookie is issued WITH Secure; on a local http request it is issued without Secure so local testing is unaffected
The cookie also sets HttpOnly and an appropriate SameSite, consistent with the remember-me/session cookies
Functional test: the cookie issued over an HTTPS(-simulated) request carries the Secure attribute; over http it does not
evidence: src/Security/TrustedDeviceManager.php: generateCookie() gains a bool $secure param passed to the Cookie $secure arg (was hardcoded false); HttpOnly kept true, SameSite=Strict kept. Sole caller TwoFactorController::challenge passes $request->isSecure().

features.title: Set trusted_hosts + require ADMIN_DOMAIN/APP_DOMAIN (fail-fast boot guard) + safe-local 2FA redirect (review C17)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C17 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). ROOT CAUSE: framework.trusted_hosts is not set (only referenced in reference.php), so the app trusts any client-supplied Host header. Visible symptom (C17): TwoFactorChallengeListener:122 stores $request->getUri() (absolute, host taken from the Host header) and TwoFactorController:157 redirects there after 2FA. MORE SERIOUS sibling of the same root cause: password-reset/verify-email links are generated with ABSOLUTE_URL during the request (PasswordResetController:64, AdminPasswordResetService:43) from the request Host, so an attacker POSTing forgot-password with a spoofed Host can make the VICTIM's reset email link to an attacker host (password-reset poisoning -> account takeover). Note router.default_uri (routing.yaml, from DEFAULT_URI) only applies in NON-HTTP contexts (workers/CLI), so it does NOT protect the current synchronous reset-email send; moving email to Messenger workers (FEATURE-104) would incidentally generate those links from DEFAULT_URI and help, but trusted_hosts is the direct fix. DECISION (Ken, 2026-07-06 — record as an ADR when picked up): (1) Set framework.trusted_hosts to the app's real hosts, declared explicitly in ALL THREE of DEFAULT_URI (host), ADMIN_DOMAIN and APP_DOMAIN — Ken accepts this as cheap, low-churn config duplication (static deploy-time env vars, not drift-prone logic). (2) AMENDS ADR-019: ADMIN_DOMAIN and APP_DOMAIN become REQUIRED (no longer optional-empty). Add a fail-fast boot guard: the app refuses to start unless DEFAULT_URI is a valid absolute URL AND ADMIN_DOMAIN and APP_DOMAIN are both non-empty. In single-domain mode the operator sets ADMIN_DOMAIN = APP_DOMAIN = the single host. This eliminates the empty-entry footgun (an empty trusted_hosts regex matches ALL hosts, silently disabling the guard). Update .env to set ADMIN_DOMAIN/APP_DOMAIN (dev = localhost) so the app still boots; .env.test and .env.acceptance already set them. (3) Fix the 2FA redirect to store a VALIDATED LOCAL path ($request->getRequestUri(), rejecting protocol-relative //host or /\ targets) instead of the absolute getUri(), so the post-2FA redirect is same-origin by construction.
acceptance_criteria: framework.trusted_hosts is configured from the app's real hosts (DEFAULT_URI host, ADMIN_DOMAIN, APP_DOMAIN); a request with a spoofed/unknown Host header is rejected (400)
The app fails to boot with a clear error unless DEFAULT_URI is a valid absolute URL and ADMIN_DOMAIN + APP_DOMAIN are both set (amends ADR-019; single-domain sets both to the same host)
.env sets ADMIN_DOMAIN/APP_DOMAIN so dev boots; the test and acceptance envs already set them
No empty entry can reach trusted_hosts (the boot guard guarantees non-empty), so the guard cannot be silently disabled
Password-reset and verify-email links can no longer be poisoned via a spoofed Host header (functional test: forgot-password with Host: evil.com does not yield a link to evil.com)
The post-2FA redirect stores a validated LOCAL path (getRequestUri), not an absolute URL; a protocol-relative or off-host target is rejected/ignored
Functional test: a spoofed Host header is rejected, and the post-2FA redirect only ever goes to a same-origin path
evidence: AC1: config/packages/framework.yaml pins trusted_hosts: ['^%env(key:host:url:DEFAULT_URI)%$','^%env(ADMIN_DOMAIN)%$','^%env(APP_DOMAIN)%$']. Functional: GET /login with Host: evil.example.com -> 400 (SuspiciousOperation); trusted host (localhost) -> 200.

AC2/AC4: src/Kernel.php::boot() fail-fast guard throws RuntimeException (web+CLI) unless DEFAULT_URI is a valid absolute URL and ADMIN_DOMAIN+APP_DOMAIN are both non-empty, so no empty pattern can reach trusted_hosts. tests/Functional/BootGuardTest.php exercises it out-of-process via bin/console: empty ADMIN_DOMAIN / empty APP_DOMAIN / non-URL DEFAULT_URI each refuse to boot; valid config boots (4/4).
AC3: .env sets ADMIN_DOMAIN=APP_DOMAIN=localhost (dev boots); .env.test=localhost, .env.acceptance=127.0.0.1 already set; both inherit DEFAULT_URI=http://localhost.

features.title: Trusted-device 2FA-bypass cookie must be revocable and invalidated on 2FA reset (review C16)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C16 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). TrustedDeviceManager (src/Security/TrustedDeviceManager.php) issues a TRUSTED_DEVICE cookie whose value is only userId:expires under an HMAC of kernel.secret (buildCookieValue/computeHmac :69-81); isDeviceTrusted (:37) validates just userId + not-expired + HMAC. It is NOT bound to the user's current totpSecret and there is NO server-side record, so it cannot be revoked. Failure: an admin resets/re-enrolls a user's 2FA after a compromise (a spec action: 'Admin can reset any user's 2FA'), but any previously issued TRUSTED_DEVICE cookie for that userId still returns true from isDeviceTrusted until its own expiry — the attacker's device keeps skipping the 2FA challenge. Disabling 2FA, re-enrolling, and password reset likewise do not invalidate it. FIX: make trusted-device cookies invalidatable. Preferred (fits explicit/auditable + enables a user-facing 'manage/forget devices' view): a server-side trusted-devices table (per-user, revocable per device; cleared on 2FA reset/disable/re-enroll and on account deactivation per FEATURE-102). Lighter alternative: bind the cookie HMAC to a per-user '2FA epoch' (or a hash of the current totpSecret) that bumps on any 2FA reset/disable/re-enroll and on password reset, so old cookies stop validating automatically — but note this invalidates ALL devices at once and cannot do targeted per-device revocation. Coordinate with FEATURE-112 (Secure flag on the same cookie).
acceptance_criteria: Resetting or re-enrolling a user's 2FA (self-service and admin-initiated) invalidates all previously issued trusted-device cookies for that user
Disabling 2FA invalidates that user's trusted-device cookies
Deactivating/soft-deleting a user invalidates their trusted-device cookies (consistent with FEATURE-102)
If the server-side table approach is taken: a user can view and individually revoke their trusted devices
Functional test: enrol a trusted device, reset the user's 2FA, confirm the old cookie no longer skips the 2FA challenge
evidence: src/Security/TrustedDeviceManager.php: new bindingToken(User) = sha256((totpSecret ?? '') . '|' . status), folded into the kernel.secret-keyed HMAC but never stored in the cookie; isDeviceTrusted() recomputes it from the user's CURRENT state, so a cookie minted under old state stops matching once totpSecret or status changes. generateCookie()/isDeviceTrusted() widened from int userId to User (lighter alternative per ADR-028; server-side table not taken, so AC4 N/A).

AC1/AC2: self-service 2FA re-enroll rotates totpSecret (TwoFactorController) and disable nulls it; admin reset nulls the secret (AdminUserController/AdminApiUserController) — binding changes -> HMAC recompute fails -> isDeviceTrusted() false -> 2FA challenge fires again. AC3: every delete/deactivate path sets status='inactive' (consistent with FEATURE-102) -> binding changes.

src/Security/TwoFactorGuard.php:54 and src/Controller/TwoFactorController.php:161 pass the authenticated $user (was (int)$user->getId()); both call sites already hold it. Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict (FEATURE-112) unchanged.

NEW tests/Unit/Security/TrustedDeviceManagerTest.php — 8 tests: cookie trusted for current state; NOT trusted after totpSecret rotates (reset+re-enroll), after totpSecret cleared (disable), after status->inactive (deactivation); wrong-user, expired, malformed still rejected.

NEW tests/Functional/Security/TrustedDeviceTest.php::testResetting2faInvalidatesTrustedDeviceCookie — full HTTP flow: trust a device (skips 2FA), rotate the user's totpSecret (reset+re-enroll), second login redirected to app_2fa_challenge (AC5). Existing TrustedDeviceTest AC1-AC4 + FEATURE-112 Secure tests stay green (active user + stable secret -> stable binding).

features.title: Admin impersonation forges a token that skips AdminChecker (inactive admin impersonable); role demotion not reflected in live sessions (review C23)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C23 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). (1) AdminAdminManagementController::impersonateStart (:274-319) hand-builds new PostAuthenticationToken($targetAdmin, 'admin', $targetAdmin->getRoles()) and writes it straight into the admin firewall session (_security_admin, :303) and TokenStorage (:307), so it NEVER runs AdminChecker (the admin user_checker that enforces isActive()). Result: an INACTIVE admin can be impersonated into a fully working admin session — whereas the user-side impersonation (ADR-014) correctly goes through ImpersonationAuthenticator + UserChecker which blocks inactive targets. Asymmetric enforcement / privilege bypass. (2) Admin::isEqualTo compares only password hash + status, NOT roles, so DEMOTING an admin (e.g. ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN -> ROLE_ADMIN) is not reflected in that admin's existing session: a demoted superadmin keeps ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN until they log out/re-authenticate. FIX: (a) before forging the impersonation token, run the target admin through the same checks a real login applies (AdminChecker::checkPreAuth / reject when isActive() is false) so an inactive or otherwise non-loginable admin cannot be impersonated — ideally route admin impersonation through a proper authenticator mirroring the user side rather than hand-forging a token; (b) make a role change invalidate live sessions — either include a normalized roles comparison in Admin::isEqualTo (so a role change forces re-auth on the next request) or explicitly invalidate the admin's sessions on demotion; apply the same review to User if user roles ever become mutable.
acceptance_criteria: Impersonating an inactive (or otherwise non-loginable) admin is rejected — the admin impersonation path runs the same checks as a normal admin login (AdminChecker)
Admin impersonation no longer injects a hand-forged token that skips the user_checker (routed through a proper authenticator, or gated by the same checks first)
Demoting an admin (e.g. removing ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN) is reflected in their live session promptly — the demoted admin loses the elevated role without needing to log out
Functional test: attempting to impersonate an inactive admin is rejected
Functional test: demoting a superadmin who has a live session removes ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN from that session on the next request
evidence: src/Controller/AdminAdminManagementController.php: impersonateStart injects App\Security\AdminChecker and runs checkPreAuth($targetAdmin) before forging the PostAuthenticationToken; on any AuthenticationException fails closed (error flash + redirect to app_admin_superadmin_admins, no token, no _impersonating_admin_* markers, no audit row) — AC1/AC2/AC4.

src/Entity/Admin.php: isEqualTo now also compares a normalized (sorted) roles list alongside password + status, so a role change makes ContextListener::hasUserChanged true and deauthenticates the stale token on the next request — AC3/AC5.

NEW tests/Functional/Security/AdminImpersonationAuthzTest.php — 2 tests / 8 assertions: testImpersonatingInactiveAdminIsRejected (inactive target -> 302 back to admins list, error flash, no impersonation banner) and testDemotingSuperadminDropsRoleInLiveSession (demoted superadmin's next request to the ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN-only page bounces to /admin/login).

Reviewer independently confirmed both tests genuinely fail on the pre-fix code (without checkPreAuth the inactive target authenticates; without the isEqualTo roles compare the stale ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN token keeps the management page reachable).
bin/verify-fast.sh: '=== All checks passed ===' — full suite OK (499 tests, 1791 assertions); anti-cheat scan clean. Impersonation regression watch OK (9 tests, 19 assertions).
Decision recorded in ADR-025. No schema change, no new config key.

features.title: Impersonation exit must not unserialize a session-stored token — restore original admin by identifier + re-auth (review C18)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C18 (.agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). On superadmin->admin impersonation EXIT, ImpersonationController::exitAdminImpersonation (:70) calls unserialize() on the _original_admin_token session value with NO allowed_classes, to restore the original superadmin security token. Rated LOW because the session is server-side (PdoSessionHandler, ADR-002) so the blob is not client-manipulable — but it is a latent deserialization-gadget amplifier: any future bug that lets an attacker write into the session would escalate from session-write to RCE, and it violates the app-code serialization standard (app code never calls serialize()/unserialize(); json_encode for data; for identities store an identifier and rehydrate via the provider). The serialized object is unnecessary: the original superadmin identifier is ALREADY in the session as a plain string _impersonating_admin_by (set from getUserIdentifier() at AdminAdminManagementController:297). FIX: on exit, drop the unserialize — read _impersonating_admin_by, load the Admin via the admin user provider, mint a fresh PostAuthenticationToken and set it on TokenStorage (let ContextListener persist _security_admin), and DELETE the _original_admin_token stash (AdminAdminManagementController:295) plus the serialize()/unserialize() calls entirely. Validate + fail closed: if the identifier is missing/'unknown' or the admin no longer loads (disabled/deleted mid-impersonation), do NOT restore — force a clean re-login. Shares the impersonation token surface with FEATURE-133 (C23, start-side forged token skipping AdminChecker); coordinate.
acceptance_criteria: ImpersonationController::exitAdminImpersonation no longer calls unserialize() (nor serialize()) — no app-code (un)serialize remains in the impersonation flow

The original superadmin is restored by loading the Admin via the admin user provider from the _impersonating_admin_by identifier and setting a fresh token on TokenStorage (ContextListener persists _security_admin)
The _original_admin_token session stash is removed — no serialized token is written at impersonation start (AdminAdminManagementController:295/303)

Fail-closed: if the stored identifier is absent/'unknown' or the admin can no longer be loaded, exit does NOT restore a token and the admin is sent to a clean (re-)login rather than a stale/forged session
Functional test: a superadmin impersonates an admin, exits, and lands back as the original superadmin (correct identity + roles) with no unserialize involved
Functional test: if the original superadmin is disabled/deleted during impersonation, exit fails closed (no restored admin session)
evidence: src/Controller/ImpersonationController.php — exitAdminImpersonation replaces the unserialize($_original_admin_token) restore block with: read _impersonating_admin_by, load the Admin via the injected admin user provider (security.user.provider.concrete.app_admins, #[Autowire]) and mint a fresh PostAuthenticationToken on TokenStorage; ContextListener persists _security_admin. No serialize()/unserialize() remains in the flow (AC1, AC2); unused TokenInterface import dropped.

src/Controller/AdminAdminManagementController.php — impersonate start no longer writes the _original_admin_token stash nor the manual _security_admin = serialize($newToken); the target token is set only via $tokenStorage->setToken(...) (ContextListener persists it). _impersonating_admin_by (plain identifier) unchanged (AC3).

Fail-closed: absent/'unknown' identifier, UserNotFoundException (deleted admin), or !isActive() (disabled admin) => setToken(null) + remove _security_admin + redirect to app_admin_login; no stale/forged session survives (AC4).

NEW tests/Functional/Security/AdminImpersonationExitTest.php — testExitRestoresOriginalSuperadmin (impersonate an admin, exit, superadmin-only /admin/superadmin/admins reachable 200 = identity+roles restored, banner gone) (AC5) and testExitFailsClosedWhenOriginalSuperadminDisabled (superadmin set inactive mid-impersonation => exit 302 -> /admin/login and a subsequent superadmin-only request bounces to login = no live admin token) (AC6).

Reviewer independently re-ran AdminImpersonationExitTest + AdminImpersonateAdminTest -> OK (5 tests, 15 assertions; the logged AccessDeniedHttpException is the fail-closed test's expected redirect) and bin/verify-fast.sh -> '=== All checks passed ===', full suite OK (486 tests, 1746 assertions), anti-cheat scan clean. REVIEW_PASS (2026-07-06), 6/6 ACs met.

features.title: Validate status and back the free-string type fields (actorType/outcome/user_type) with enums/allowlist (review C33)
features.description: Code review 2026-07-06, finding C33 (see .agent/CODE_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). setStatus() on User (:145-149) and Admin (:117-121) accepts ANY string, while setRoles() already enforces an allowlist — so a write path can persist status='banned' or other garbage; the allowed set ['active','inactive'] currently lives only as a private const duplicated across three controllers (AdminAdminManagementController, AdminUserController, AdminApiUserController), not on the entity. Status is now load-bearing (soft-delete sets status='inactive' per FEATURE-110; Admin/User::isEqualTo compares status; login rejects non-active), so an invalid value is a real data-integrity risk. Other type-like fields are also unbacked free strings: AuditLog actorType ('user'/'admin'), AuditLog outcome ('success'/'failure'), user_sessions user_type. FIX: give status a single validated source — a PHP 8.1 backed enum (active|inactive) or an entity-level allowlist mirroring setRoles() — enforced in setStatus() on BOTH User and Admin, and delete the duplicated per-controller consts. Recommended (fits the explicit/auditable preference): backed enums for status, actorType, and outcome (and user_type), so invalid values are impossible at the type level. Ties to FEATURE-115 (C22: reject invalid status on edit).
acceptance_criteria: setStatus() on User and Admin rejects any value outside the allowed set (active/inactive) — no arbitrary string is persistable
The allowed-status set has a single source (backed enum or entity constant), not a per-controller private const
AuditLog actorType and outcome (and user_sessions user_type) are backed by enums or a validated allowlist rather than free strings
Existing status/actorType/outcome/user_type values still round-trip correctly (no data breakage)
Unit test: setStatus('banned') is rejected; a valid status is accepted

src/Entity/User.php + src/Entity/Admin.php — setStatus() throws \InvalidArgumentException on any value outside AccountStatus (default-deny, mirrors setRoles()); no arbitrary string is persistable (AC1).
src/Entity/AuditLog.php — setActorType() validates vs PrincipalType, setOutcome() vs AuditOutcome; src/Entity/UserSession.php — setUserType() validates vs PrincipalType (AC3).

The three duplicated private ALLOWED_STATUSES consts (AdminAdminManagementController, AdminUserController, Api/AdminApiUserController) deleted; every in_array(...ALLOWED_STATUSES) replaced with AccountStatus::isValid() — behaviour identical (AC2).

AC4 (no data breakage) met by construction: columns stay string (no schema change, no migration); the $status default is a property initializer and Doctrine hydrates via reflection, so setters aren't invoked on load; every write-path call site passes a valid value (reviewer audited all setStatus/setActorType/setOutcome/setUserType call sites in src/ — the throw is an unreachable backstop, no new 500 surface).

NEW tests/Unit/Enum/AccountStatusTest.php (covers all three enums), NEW tests/Unit/Entity/{AuditLogTest,UserSessionTest}.php, extended tests/Unit/Entity/{UserTest,AdminTest}.php — setStatus('banned') rejected + valid accepted, accept/reject for each enum (AC5).

features.title: Root path '/' must redirect (login when anonymous, landing when authenticated), not serve Symfony's default 404 welcome page
features.description: Discovered 2026-07-06 while diagnosing an init.sh 'did not respond' warning. There is NO controller/route for the root path '/': GET http://auth.localhost/ returns the framework's default 'Welcome to Symfony!' page with HTTP 404 (no route matches). Expected behaviour for an auth boilerplate: hitting '/' should redirect an unauthenticated visitor to the login page (/login) and an already-authenticated user to the post-login landing page (the same destination the app uses after login, e.g. the account/dashboard home) rather than dead-ending on a 404 welcome page. Add a root controller/route that performs this redirect based on the user's authentication state on the user firewall. NOTE (symptom, not the fix): .agent/bin/init.sh's local URL check does `curl -fsS $BASE_URL` against '/', and because '/' currently 404s, the -f (--fail) flag makes it print 'Warning: auth.localhost did not respond' even though the server is healthy (/login returns 200). Once '/' redirects (2xx/3xx), that false warning disappears; no separate init.sh change is required, though pointing the check at a known-good path would also be acceptable.
acceptance_criteria: GET / for an unauthenticated visitor issues a redirect to the login page (not a 404, not the Symfony welcome page)
GET / for an authenticated user redirects to the app's post-login landing page (consistent with the post-login destination)
No request to '/' returns the default 'Welcome to Symfony!' framework page
Functional test: anonymous GET / redirects to /login; authenticated GET / redirects to the landing page
As a consequence, .agent/bin/init.sh's local URL check no longer emits a false 'did not respond' warning (or the check targets a known-good path)
evidence: NEW src/Controller/RootController.php — #[Route('/', name: 'app_root')]; getUser()!==null -> redirectToRoute('app_dashboard'), else -> redirectToRoute('app_login'). Both branches 302, so '/' never serves the Symfony welcome/404 page.
app_dashboard (/dashboard) is the user firewall's default_target_path (security.yaml:75), so authed '/' matches the real post-login destination (AC2).

NEW tests/Functional/Navigation/RootRedirectTest.php — 3 tests / 6 assertions: anonymous GET / -> 302 /login (AC1); authenticated GET / (real form login) -> 302 /dashboard (AC2/AC4); anonymous GET / asserts 302 AND no 'Welcome to Symfony' text (AC3).
AC5 by consequence: '/' now returns 302 (<400), so init.sh's `curl -fsS` (no -L) exits 0 — no init.sh change needed; init.sh left untouched.

Reviewer independently re-ran RootRedirectTest -> OK (3 tests, 6 assertions); bin/verify-fast.sh -> '=== All checks passed ===', full suite OK (452 tests, 1598 assertions), anti-cheat scan clean. REVIEW_PASS (2026-07-06), 5/5 ACs met.

features.description: C36 prerequisite (Ken, 2026-07-07): before extracting any bundle, establish a trustworthy green benchmark, since the whole reason C36 waited for the fix phase is to detect extraction regressions against a suite you trust. features.description: C36 Option A, INCREMENTAL (Ken, 2026-07-07): build the spec's optional-bundle architecture for real, one bundle first to establish the pattern before the harder User-mutating ones. features.title: Unified prune harness: app:prune + tagged auth.pruner contributors (closes C11 residue)
features.description: Design in /home/vboxuser/.claude/plans/c11-residue-invitations-and-merry-deer.md (Ken, 2026-07-09). C11 re-verification left two tables with no keep/prune decision (invitations, webhook_delivery). Replace the two bare prune commands (app:audit-log:prune, app:maintenance:prune) with ONE app:prune harness that collects PrunerInterface contributors via #[AutoconfigureTag('auth.pruner')] + #[AutowireIterator] (same extension pattern as ConfigPageProviderInterface/ConfigPageRegistry, so bundle pruners are tagged only when their bundle is registered — modularity falls out free, no services.php/compiler-pass edits). Each pruner owns its domain predicate + reads its own retention via ConfigService; the harness owns infra (sorting, dry-run, per-pruner error isolation, one audit row). DECISIONS: invitations prune when (expired OR used) AND older than invitation.retention_days (default 30; threshold = usedAt ?? expiresAt) — invitations are NOT logs, history belongs to the audit log (admin.user_invite rows already exist); webhook_delivery prunes attemptedAt older than webhook.delivery_retention_days (default 30, all statuses); messenger failed queue stays operator-owned (messenger:failed:remove, documented, NOT a pruner); NO locking/batching (rejected with revisit triggers). Legacy commands + tests DELETED, but only after carrying every scenario into the new functional PruneCommandTest (anti-cheat: consolidation not weakening). NOTE: the plan says 'New ADR-047' but ADR-047 was just taken by the /admin-api decision this session — use the next free number (ADR-048) for the harness ADR.
acceptance_criteria: src/Prune/PrunerInterface.php exists (#[AutoconfigureTag('auth.pruner')]) with name()/count(\DateTimeImmutable)/prune(\DateTimeImmutable); count() is a pure dry-run (mutates nothing); each pruner reads its own retention config internally
A single app:prune command (PruneCommand) collects all auth.pruner-tagged pruners via #[AutowireIterator], runs them sorted by name(), and prints per-pruner counts + a total summary
--dry-run calls count() only (never prune(), never audit-logs); --only=<name> filters (repeatable); an unknown --only name errors listing available names and exits 1; duplicate pruner names throw
Per-pruner error isolation: a throwing pruner is reported and the rest still run; overall exit is FAILURE if any pruner failed

Core pruners exist and prune correctly: audit_log (createdAt < now - audit_log.retention_days, default 90), password_reset_tokens + admin_password_reset_tokens (expired-or-used), user_sessions (dead vs sessions lifetime), invitations ((expired OR used) AND (usedAt ?? expiresAt) < now - invitation.retention_days default 30)

features.title: Admin session teardown on soft-delete/deactivate + admin_sessions pruner (records the admin remember-me precondition)
features.description: Review residue (Ken, 2026-07-09). Per ADR-020 admin 'delete' is a soft delete (status='inactive'); AdminAdminManagementController::delete() flips the status but never touches the admin_sessions bookkeeping table, so the deleted admin's row(s) linger as ghost 'active sessions' in /admin/sessions forever: rows are removed only on explicit logout (which a deauthenticated admin never performs) and — unlike user_sessions, which FEATURE-147 gave a pruner — admin_sessions has NO pruner at all, so ghosts (including rows from admins who simply closed the browser) never age out. This is bookkeeping-only TODAY: the deleted admin genuinely loses access via Admin::isEqualTo status comparison (next-request deauth), AdminChecker (no re-login), and AdminTokenAuthenticator (API tokens rejected). Mirror the user realm's pattern: (a) tear down admin_sessions whenever admin management transitions an admin to inactive (delete or edit-to-inactive) — AdminSessionRepository::deleteAllByAdminId() already exists; (b) add a core AdminSessionPruner (auth.pruner, name 'admin_sessions') mirroring UserSessionPruner, keyed on the PdoSessionHandler sessions-table lifetime. CRITICAL PRECONDITION TO RECORD (Ken plans to add admin remember-me eventually): today's 'cosmetic only' verdict depends on the admin firewall having NO remember_me. The user realm kills remember-me on delete/deactivate/terminate-all by bumping sessionsInvalidatedAt, folded into the cookie HMAC (ConfigAwareRememberMeHandler); Admin has no such field. Any future admin remember-me feature MUST add the equivalent marker on Admin, bind it into the cookie HMAC, and bump it in this teardown — otherwise review finding C3 (revoked access survives via remember-me) reopens in the admin realm. The ADR for this feature must state that precondition so the tripwire discipline carries it forward.
acceptance_criteria: Transitioning an admin to status='inactive' via admin management (delete route AND edit-to-inactive) deletes all of that admin's admin_sessions rows in the same flow as the status change (AdminSessionRepository::deleteAllByAdminId)

Functional test: a logged-in admin who is soft-deleted by a superadmin is bounced to /admin/login on their next request AND their admin_sessions rows are gone (assert the row deletion explicitly — Admin::isEqualTo deauth alone must not be the only thing making the test pass)

Core AdminSessionPruner exists (implements PrunerInterface, tagged auth.pruner, name 'admin_sessions'), pruning rows whose session id is absent from or expired in the PdoSessionHandler sessions table, mirroring UserSessionPruner; AdminSessionRepository gains deleteExpired/countExpired with identical predicates (dry-run honesty)
app:prune output includes 'admin_sessions'; functional PruneCommandTest gains seed/prune coverage for it (live session survives, expired + orphan rows pruned, idempotent second run reports 0)

An ADR (next free number, or an ADR-034 amendment) records the teardown + pruner AND the admin remember-me precondition (future admin remember_me MUST add a sessionsInvalidatedAt-equivalent marker on Admin bound into the cookie HMAC and bumped by this teardown, else C3 reopens in the admin realm); Tripwire line tagged verifiable citing the tests above
bin/verify-fast.sh green; no test skipped, weakened, or deleted
evidence: AC1 (teardown on transition to inactive, delete AND edit-to-inactive): AdminAdminManagementController::delete() (always→inactive) and edit() (guarded by $status==='inactive') both call AdminSessionRepository::deleteAllByAdminId((int)$admin->getId()) in the same flow as the status flip; the existing repo method is reused (no new deletion path).

features.description: Ken (2026-07-09): maintainers need superadmin access without appearing on clients' staff lists. New admin role ROLE_TECH_SUPPORT = ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN via role_hierarchy, but accounts holding it are hidden from all admin-management surfaces for non-tech-support viewers (superadmins included); tech-support admins see everyone, each other included.
