features.title: Htaccess Lock: tech-support-only, web-server-level IP-whitelist lock managed from the admin panel
features.description: Ken (2026-09-30): internal back-office tools should not be wide open. A tech-support-only admin page (sidebar: Maintainer -> Htaccess Lock) edits a managed block of public/.htaccess to enforce a whitelist-only policy (Apache/LiteSpeed, `Require ip`). Settings: on/off radio; allowed IPs/CIDRs (one per line); exempt URL paths (one per line, trailing * = prefix) reachable from any IP; blocked status 403 or a real (fake) 404; optional error file (blank = empty body). Plus a separate enforcement self-test that inserts/removes the server's own IP via loopback requests and restores the original file. Decisions: TECH-SUPPORT ONLY (not even superadmin); only the marked block is edited; strict input grammar (no directive injection); self-lockout guard; console recovery command app:htaccess-lock:disable; new core feature (no table, config-store backed) rather than a bundle. See ADR-059.
acceptance_criteria: Only ROLE_TECH_SUPPORT can view or use the page and its POST actions (superadmin gets 403, anonymous is sent to login); the sidebar link appears for tech-support only

Saving with the lock ON writes a managed, marker-delimited block at the top of the .htaccess (Require ip per whitelist entry, exempt paths via env, configured status/error file) and leaves the rest of the file byte-for-byte intact; OFF removes only that block
IPv4, IPv6 and CIDR entries are accepted and canonicalised; any line containing anything else (directive smuggling, /0, bad prefix, hostnames) is rejected and nothing is written
Exempt paths use a strict URL-path alphabet; `/*` is rejected; trailing `*` renders a prefix match
Blocked status is 403 or a real 404; error file must exist under the web root; blank means an empty body
Enabling is refused (422, nothing written) when the admin's own IP is not covered by the whitelist or the whitelist is empty

A self-test runs loopback requests proving: not-whitelisted -> blocked, exempt path -> allowed, server IP inserted -> allowed, configured status honoured; it restores the original .htaccess byte-for-byte on pass, fail, error or unreachable site, and fails loudly on a server that ignores .htaccess
app:htaccess-lock:disable removes the block from the shell and records the lock as off, keeping the saved whitelist
Saves and self-tests are audit-logged (outcome + counts, not the IPs); CSRF is enforced on both POST actions
Generated directives verified against a real Apache 2.4 (all four status/body shapes, CIDR allow, exact + prefix exemption, coexistence with existing rewrite rules)
evidence: tests/Unit/Htaccess: 52 tests — validator (canonicalisation, 10 bad-IP and 9 bad-path injection cases, /0, status, error file, lockout guard), renderer (exact text for all status/body combos, exempt patterns), file editor (prepend/replace/remove byte-for-byte, unbalanced markers refused, atomic write keeps perms, snapshot/restore incl. absence), self-test (enforcing server passes; ignoring/500/unreachable/probe-throws all fail loudly and restore the file; unwritable file stops before any request)

features.title: Htaccess Lock changes are serialised: concurrent changes are never lost (issue #44)
features.description: HtaccessLockGate::mutate()/disable() did an unserialised read-modify-write of the whole policy and the manager wrote five config rows with no transaction, so two concurrent changes each started from the same snapshot and the last writer won (a revoked IP silently came back; an added one was dropped), and file/config writes could interleave. The gate now runs read -> derive -> validate -> write (and the self-test's swap/restore) inside HtaccessLockMutex (exclusive flock on its own lock file), settings() reads the rows fresh from the DB, and save() writes them straight to the DB in one DBAL transaction (not via ConfigService, whose identity map skipped writes equal to a stale loaded value) and refreshes loaded entities.
